sections.label: Shipowners' Liens and Schemes Amendments
sections.summary: Two amendments exempt Shipowners' Liens from charge registration and clarify who is bound by a compromise or scheme of arrangement during winding up.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The first amendment seeks to exempt Shipowners' Liens from the requirement of registration as a charge under the Companies Act.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The second amendment seeks to clarify the categories of persons bound by a compromise or scheme of arrangement when a company is in the course of being wound up.

sections.label: Saving Unregistered Shipowners' Liens
sections.summary: Clause 2 preserves, where possible, the validity of unregistered Shipowners' Liens existing before the amendment comes into force.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Clause 2 contains a saving provision that preserves, where possible, the validity of unregistered Shipowners' Liens existing prior to this amendment coming into force.

sections.label: Reinstating Creditors and Members
sections.summary: Clause 3 is a technical amendment reinstating creditors and members bound by a compromise or scheme of arrangement before the 2014 amendments.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In 2014, the provision was amended to clarify that holders of units of shares in a company can be parties to a compromise or scheme of arrangement.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: However, creditors and members, who were bound by a compromise or scheme of arrangement before the amendments in 2014, were inadvertently excluded from the amended provision, in respect of a company which is in the course of being wound up.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Thus, clause 3 is a technical amendment to reinstate these categories of persons.

sections.label: Registering Liens Impractical
sections.summary: The speaker agrees it is impractical to require registration of liens for freights, hire, sub-freights or sub-hire, and failure may lead to penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Moreover, many charterparties and fixture notes have Singapore or Singapore law as part of their jurisdiction or arbitration or governing law clauses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I agree that it is wholly impractical to require all liens for freights, hire, sub-freights or sub-hire to be registered as charges under sections 131(f) or (g) of the Companies Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If the law is not amended, businesses may be compelled to register charges for such liens, and failure to do so may even lead to penalties under the Companies Act.

sections.label: Comparing Shipowners' Lien Law
sections.summary: The amendments should place Singapore's law on shipowners' lien in a better position than Hong Kong or the UK.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The amendments should, in my view, now place our law on shipowners’ lien in a better position than Hong Kong or the UK.

sections.label: Court of Appeal Recommendation Response
sections.summary: The Court of Appeal rightly recommended the changes, a swift legislative response to its proposal in Diablo Fortune Inc vs Duncan, Cameron Lindsay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Court of Appeal was certainly right to recommend the proposed changes to Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is a swift legislative response to the Court of Appeal's proposal in the case of Diablo Fortune Inc vs Duncan, Cameron Lindsay, as the Minister has pointed out, to carve out liens on sub-freights from the registration requirement under section 131(1) of the Companies Act.

sections.label: Transition for lien non-registration
sections.summary: New section 131(3AC) makes non-registration consequences apply only before the amendments commence where there is a liquidator or creditor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 131(3AC) provides for a period of transition by clarifying that the consequences of non-registration should only apply prior to the amendments commencing where there is a liquidator or creditor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Until the new amendments take effect, under section 132(1) of the Companies Act, the lienor or company and every officer of the company is guilty of an offence and liable to a fine for not registering such a lien.

sections.label: When liens become registrable
sections.summary: New subsection 3AC makes a lien registrable only if the company is wound up or a creditor has acquired a proprietary right or interest.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: New subsection 3AC provides that the lien will be regarded as registrable and be subject to the consequences of non-registration only if: as at the effective date of the amendments, the company has been wound up; or a creditor has acquired a proprietary right to, or an interest in the subject matter of the Lien.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, in other words, it is only in those two situations – the company has been wound up or a creditor has acquired a proprietary right to or interest in – that it will become registrable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Therefore, a large majority of the existing Liens will not be registrable and, hence, no offence would be committed.

sections.label: Commonsense approach to commencement
sections.summary: The government will take a commonsense approach and work to bring the amendments' commencement date into effect as soon as possible.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In short, we will take a commonsense approach and also, assuming that the Bill is passed today, we will work to bring the commencement date of the amendments into effect as soon as possible.
